newsitem.title: UK: Claim prize, British lottery urges unknown winner.
newsitem.headline: Claim prize, British lottery urges unknown winner.

text.p: Britain's lottery made a final effort on Thursday to make someone into a millionaire, urging a retiring ticket holder to speak now or lose the lot.
It even sent a plane over Hull -- the English town where the lucky ticket was bought in May -- trailing a huge banner in the hope of catching the prize-winner's attention.
"Two million prize -- is it you?" read the banner, which fluttered over Hull for three hours.

"So far nobody has claimed and unfortunately it looks like it may stay that way. But we're certainly keeping our fingers crossed that someone will get in touch," said Alison Howard, a spokeswoman for Camelot, the national lottery operator.
Howard said the winner had until 2300 GMT to claim the 2.1 million pounds ($3.54 million) or else the money would go to "good causes" such as sports, the arts or charity.

"It's impossible to tell why the winner has not come forward. It could be someone has misplaced the ticket. Maybe it's in a coat pocket. Maybe someone knows and doesn't want the money. Who knows?" said Howard.
A letter was sent last week to a local paper purporting to be from an 89-year-old widow who had the ticket but did not want the money. Howard said Camelot had not heard from the woman.
